question: Can a ReviewGraphen-first code review produce a valid bounded artifact when the agent is not asked to enumerate obligations first and is given explicit convergence constraints?

predecessor.reviewgraphen_observation: The exact first tool call was reviewgraphen-context lower_compose, but the four-file task timed out at 5400 seconds with no review.json after 107447 provider output tokens.
predecessor.control_diagnostic_observation: The current-server no-ReviewGraphen diagnostic also timed out at 5400 seconds with no review.json after 58935 provider output tokens.
predecessor.diagnosis_under_test: Open review scope plus no explicit convergence policy allowed repeated source re-reading and final-check loops; projection use alone did not force artifact production.

task.scope: lower_compose and helpers it directly uses in compose.rs only
task.existing_methodology_skill_exclusion_rea: It explicitly forbids ReviewGraphen tool use and requires obligations to be enumerated before defect review.

intervention.post_checkpoint_policy: validate, refine, or remove existing findings only; no new hypothesis or scope expansion
intervention.insufficient_budget_policy: keep a schema-valid artifact, record limitation, and stop

execution.completion: agent exits zero, source is unchanged, report validates, first tool is compliant, tool-call/checkpoint bounds pass, and no truncated tail is detected

quality.judge: A valid candidate is judged blind by Codex gpt-5.6-sol high using issue-worthiness, source support, and bounded-scope compliance.
quality.no_candidate: If no valid report exists, Codex is not called and the run remains an execution failure.
